acceptance: Decided semantics for clustering + sorting on one PostgreSQL table, recorded in the registry note and the platform docs
Ledger and reconciliation match the decision: no generic 'adapter rendered no statement' drop for this case
Unit test for the combined case
context: Implemented in PR #3123 (branch fix/postgres-cluster-sort-reconciliation, commit 58308bc5b rebased): reconciliation recognizes sort columns as secondary ordering after the same table's clustering columns in the combined index; unrelated sorts still drop; 5 new tests, broader tuning suite 1534 passed. PR armed 2026-10-18; after merge, take and finish.
description: Since #3092 (6dc8cdc74), PostgreSQL builds one index on the clustering columns followed by the sorting columns and runs CLUSTER on it (PostgreSQLDDLGenerator.generate_tuning_clauses in benchbox/core/tuning/generators/postgresql.py; PostgreSQLAdapter.postgres_layout_statements and apply_post_load_tunings in benchbox/platforms/postgresql.py). Reconciliation matches a sort intent only when its columns are a prefix of a recorded index (benchbox/core/tuning/reconciliation.py _shows, _INDEX_COLUMNS). So a table that requests both records the sort intent as dropped ("adapter rendered no statement"), even though the table is physically ordered by clustering then sort columns. Documented in docs/platforms/postgresql.md as a limitation. Decide the intended semantics: order by sort columns first, a dedicated reason, or a validation warning.
